jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invite applications for a tenure-track DIAS Fellow position at Assistant Professor level in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment, with a focus on input-output life cycle assessment methods and big data. The candidate is expected to start during the summer/early fall in 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, in agreement with the successful candidate. 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Who are we looking for?

The position translates this ambition into a concrete research agenda, because many of the most pressing sustainability questions, such as how consumption in one country drives resource use, emissions and social conditions in another, or how a new technology changes environmental impacts across whole economies, cannot be answered within a single discipline. Industrial ecology addresses these questions by tracing material, energy and monetary flows through global supply chains, drawing on methods and data from engineering, economics and the natural and social sciences. Input-output analysis, built on big data covering production, trade, emissions and resource use and combined with life cycle assessment and material flow analysis, provides the quantitative framework for linking decisions about individual products, technologies and policies to their economy-wide consequences. The Fellow will build this capacity at SDU and use DIAS as a platform to work with researchers in fields such as health, food, energy, economics and political science on questions that cross disciplinary boundaries. Within this ambition, the specific profile is as follows.

We seek an early-career researcher who will advance quantitative sustainability assessment within industrial ecology by developing data-driven environmental-economic and systems models that link global production and consumption to environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. The role includes independent research, research-based teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration across DIAS and the Department, and development of competitive external funding proposals. Relevant research themes include:

·         environmental and material footprinting of global production and consumption systems;

·         development and application of environmentally extended input–output (EEIO) and multi-regional input–output (MRIO) models and databases, including hybrid physical–monetary systems and transparent, reproducible data workflows;

·         hybrid modelling that combines EEIO analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA), material flow analysis (MFA), econometrics or other quantitative methods;

·         applications to food and resource systems, healthcare systems and medical technologies, the circular economy, energy, infrastructure and other societal systems; and

·         scenario, structural decomposition, uncertainty and econometric analysis for sustainability transitions, policy and decision support.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

·         A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

·         A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields.

·         Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

·         Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must:

·         Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of industrial ecology, environmental or ecological economics, environmental science or engineering, sustainability science or a closely related field. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

·         The successful candidate should demonstrate strong competence in EEIO or MRIO analysis, and at least one of the following areas: LCA, MFA, or hybrid modelling; econometric, statistical, or other quantitative methods; and programming, data science, or management of large, heterogeneous datasets.

·         Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries.

·         Be fluent in English.

·         Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

·         Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.   

The Department of Green Technology

The Department of Green Technology at SDU is a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment focused on developing technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Our research spans environmental chemistry, process engineering, life cycle thinking, and circular systems. We collaborate closely with industry and public stakeholders to ensure real-world impact and relevance.

This position will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering (SDU LCE).

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

SDU LCE uses industrial ecology approaches to reduce environmental impacts and reconcile human development with environmental stewardship. We conduct holistic systems analyses and design studies to characterise and optimise engineering solutions over the long term, considering resource use, energy efficiency, climate and environmental impacts, and economic and socioeconomic performance. At SDU LCE, we develop and apply theory, methods and tools for material flow analysis (MFA), life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle engineering, energy-system analysis and design, resource-criticality assessment, process integration and techno-economic assessment.

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For further information about SDU Life Cycle Engineering and this position, please contact Head of Centre, Professor Morten Birkved, at morb@igt.sdu.dk.

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please see Further information on salary and taxation.

 

The tenure track programme is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level (up to six years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential.

Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities. 

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

Please go to our website for full information on how to apply.

The application deadline is February 28, 2027, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

SDU Robotics

SDU Robotics conducts research among others within the fields of robotics and computer vision. The unit focuses on research problems from real robotics applications within manufacturing industries, hospitals, elderly care, and other partners in society. SDU Robotics’ research involves mathematical modeling and control of robots, robotic processes and robot systems, human-robot interactions, computer vision for reliable inspection and robot control, and simulation technologies for robotics and computer vision aimed at closing the Sim2Real gap. jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications for post-doctoral fellowships in human endocrinology and developmental disruption from January 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
Two fully funded 1–2-years’ postdoc positions are available at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor David M. Kristensen. The positions involve collaboration with Copenhagen University Hospital – Rigshospitalet, Harvard University (USA) and Inserm (France). The projects will focus on developing and using already established models to understand human endocrinology, disruption of development by xenobiotics and translating such data to human clinical endpoints using prospective cohorts.

Responsibilities and tasks
The work will include research within male and female endocrinology, early development, organotypic culture explants, with focus on understanding novel mechanisms of endocrine disruption during development by specific known chemicals. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of organotypic assays using human and murine tissues. 
• Lead rodent experiments to understand disruption of development. 
• Apply standard molecular approaches to characterize RNA and protein expression in cells and tissue samples.
• Analyse and possibly validate candidate biomarkers relevant to developmental disruption using plasma and other biofluid samples from relevant cohorts or models.
• Contribute with mentoring pre-graduate and PhD students within the focus of the research project.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of research accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals.
• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in developmental biology is required.

• Experience with research in endocrinology and endocrine disruption will be an advantage. 
The ideal candidate should be enterprising and possess good communication skills, be visible and involved in the group’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department and with project collaborators in Denmark and abroad.

The Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Southern Denmark (SDU, Campus Vejle), invites applications for postdoctoral fellowships in Computer Science, with an emphasis on Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development and development and Engineering.

We welcome applications from researchers interested in areas that include, but are not limited to:

• 
Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Developent, including approaches to improving the sustainability, efficiency, and reliability of software systems.

• 
Cloud and Distributed Computing, including cloud and edge computing, Internet of Things, microservices, serverless architectures, and web technologies.

The targeted starting period is Spring 2027, with room for flexibility.

Whom we are looking for
We are looking for motivated candidates interested in pursuing postdoctoral research in Computer Science, particularly within the research areas relevant to SustainAI.

Applicants should possess, or be nearing completion of, an PhD degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Processing Science, Advanced-Systems Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Ideal candidates demonstrate strong academic performance, research potential, and motivation to pursue scientific research.

Experience or demonstrated interest in empirical research methods, AI-driven software engineering, software architecture, formal methods, cloud-native systems, or software sustainability is particularly relevant. However, applicants with complementary expertise that can strengthen or expand SustainAI's research activities are equally encouraged to apply.

Fluency in English is required.

Candidates who have not yet completed their qualifying degree must obtain it before taking up the respective position.

Hosting environment
The position will be part of the the Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) located in Vejle. 
SustainAI is a research group within the Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark's Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA). 

SustainAI conducts research at the intersection of software engineering, artificial intelligence, and sustainability, with the ambition of advancing the development, operation, and evolution of intelligent, reliable, and sustainable software systems.
The group's research encompasses empirical software engineering, software architecture, software quality, AI-driven software development, cloud-native technologies, and the application of emerging AI techniques to software engineering challenges.

SustainAI combines foundational and empirical research with practical applications, promoting collaboration with international academic partners, industry, and public organisations. Its activities aim to advance software engineering knowledge and practices while addressing emerging technological, environmental, and societal challenges.

The group is part of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence at Campus Vejle, offering opportunities for interdisciplinary research, international collaboration, and professional development.
More information about SustainAI can be found at https://sustainai.sdu.dk/. 

The Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA).
The section brings together research and education in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, programming languages, and software engineering. Its activities focus on developing intelligent, secure, reliable, and sustainable software systems, combining fundamental research with practical applications and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Research within ACP addresses topics such as AI-driven software development, software architecture and evolution, programming language technologies, formal methods, distributed computing, cybersecurity, software quality, and trustworthy AI.
The section promotes collaboration with industry, public organisations, and international research partners to address emerging technological and societal challenges. Through its research, teaching, and knowledge-transfer activities, ACP contributes to advancing the foundations and engineering practices of modern computing systems while educating the next generation of computer science professionals and researchers.
More information about the section is available at https://acp.sdu.dk/.

The section is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science which offers an inclusive and international working environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong traditions of collaboration across research groups, departments, and faculties, as well as with external organisations, including educational institutions, municipalities, and companies.
The degrees offered by the department include BSc and MSc degrees in Computer Science, a BSc degree in Artificial Intelligence, and an MSc degree in Data Science.

jobs.occupation: PhD position: Development and Validation of Novel Antifungal Polyene Macrolides
jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (BMB), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), Odense, invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship within the field of membrane biophysics and antifungal drug research. The project, Development and validation of novel antifungal polyene macrolides, will be carried out in the group of Daniel Wüstner. The position is to be filled from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project
Fungal infections are a growing threat to human health, and only few classes of antifungal drugs are available. Polyene macrolides such as nystatin, natamycin and amphotericin B act by interacting with ergosterol, the main sterol of fungal membranes, but their precise mode of action is still poorly understood. This limits the rational design of new, more selective and less toxic polyenes.
The aim of this PhD project is to develop and validate novel antifungal polyene macrolides. The PhD student will characterize how new polyene variants interact with sterol-containing model membranes and with living yeast cells. Key methods include UV-sensitive and quantitative fluorescence microscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and biophysical assays of membrane permeability, etc. The project will be carried out in close collaboration with national and international partners.

Your profile
You have a master's degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, biophysics, chemistry or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with documented experience in:

• 
Fluorescence microscopy

• 
Fluorescence and/or absorption spectroscopy

• 
Working with model membranes, such as liposomes or giant unilamellar vesicles

Experience with yeast as a model organism will be considered an advantage.
You are a team player with a positive attitude, and at the same time you are able to work independently and take responsibility for your own project. Good communication skills and good written and spoken English are required.

Your tasks
As a PhD student, you will:

• 
Carry out your own research project and present the results in scientific papers and a PhD thesis

• 
Take part in teaching activities at the department

• 
Follow PhD courses as part of the PhD programme

• 
Present your work at national and international conferences

• 
Contribute to the daily life and collaborations of the research group

We offer
You will join a dedicated research group with access to state-of-the-art fluorescence microscopy and spectroscopy, and a network of national and international collaborators.
The PhD scholarship is for three years, and the successful candidate will be enrolled in the PhD programme at the Faculty of Science, SDU. The place of employment is Odense.

jobs.description:
The RNA Precision Medicine Center, Section of Translational Biology, at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, the University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a PhD student position within the field of pre-mRNA splicing and disease. The position is to be filled from 1 January, 2027.

The candidate will be part of a dynamic research group, which focus on generating a better understanding of all aspects of RNA biology in human disease and how to translate this into precision medicine.
The present project is focused on pre-mRNA splicing regulatory mechanisms and how inherited mutations can cause aberrant splicing and human disease. 

More specifically, the project will investigate a new strategy for increasing expression by modulating alternative splicing of pseudoexons (PEs) in the 5′ untranslated region (5′ UTR). The project will identify SSO-modulable 5′ UTR PEs in human disease genes, focusing on CNS genes. 

In parallel, the project will investigate how disease-associated variants located upstream of coding regions may cause disease. The project aims to provide mechanistic insight into 5′ UTR splicing and uORF mediated regulation and identify specific SSO-based therapeutic opportunities. Finally, the project should establish a tool to predict pathogenic effects of upstream non-coding variants, thereby improving molecular diagnostics in clinical genetics.
Overall, the project will generate basic knowledge on RNA-centered molecular mechanisms, the molecular pathology of aberrant splicing and it aims at translating this into new precision RNA medicine.

Applications are sought from candidates with a master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, medicine or a related field and documented experience in molecular and cellular biology. 

Specifically, experimental expertise in RNA biology, including working with antisense oligonucleotides and RNA binding small molecule drugs for modulation of splicing, as well as hands-on experience with Next Generation Sequencing technologies and bioinformatics is preferable.
Applicants should have demonstrated scientific productivity, good inter-personal and communication skills, good written and spoken English skills and be able to conduct independent and creative research.

The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology offers a strong, international and competitive research environment within the fields of RNA biology, molecular genetics and cell biology, protein chemistry and mass spectrometry, molecular microbiology and biophysics.

You create clarity fast, decide when it is needed, and build trust through consistency rather than control. You read cultures well, because what works in Gedved does not automatically land in Sweden or Austria. And you like pragmatic solutions. Besides, you have:

• 
5+ years in Customer Service, Customer Operations, Sales Support or a comparable function, including people leadership, ideally across locations or countries.

• 
A proven track record of leading Customer Service through transformation: harmonizing, centralizing or integrating teams from a fragmented starting point. This is not your first change journey.

• 
Hands-on experience setting up KPIs, service levels and reporting, and implementing or optimizing Customer Service systems, preferably ticketing or case management.

• 
Solid understanding of order-to-delivery in an international B2B environment. Experience with distributor networks and manufacturing, medical devices, assistive technology or other product-driven industries is a strong plus.

• 
Professional fluency in English. Danish, Swedish or German is an advantage.

About Etac

Etac is a world-leading developer of innovative assistive devices and patient handling equipment. Since 1973, we have been committed to improving quality of life for the individual, family members and caregivers.

Through our specialised product brands, we offer state-of-the-art solutions for a wide range of daily needs and care settings, for people at all stages of life. Headquartered in Sweden, Etac is a global company with around 1 500 employees, sales in over 80 countries and a revenue of approximately EUR 500 million.
